questions.stem: When creating an alert management rule, where would you specify a workflow to resolve a given condition?
questions.explanation: In an alert management rule, the Remediation tab is where you specify a workflow to resolve a given condition. The Remediation tab contains options to launch remediation workflows or subflows that can automatically fix the issue that triggered the alert. The Actions tab handles notification and task creation, not workflow execution.

questions.stem: What types of system can a MID Server install on? (Choose two.)

options.text: Any system inside the customer firewall

questions.explanation: A MID Server can be installed on Microsoft Windows Server and Linux System platforms. These are the two supported operating systems for MID Server installation. OpenVMS, Windows Desktop, Mac OS X, and generic 'any system inside the firewall' are not supported MID Server platforms.

questions.stem: What would be the primary use case for creating Javascripts in Event Management?

options.text: To create a customized pull connector to retrieve events on behalf of an event source
To automatically populate the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
To parse a nodename out of your raw event data in an event rule
To run as part of a remediation workflow for IT alerts that fail to execute

questions.explanation: The primary use case for creating JavaScript in Event Management is to parse a nodename out of raw event data in an event rule. In the Transform and Compose tab of an event rule, JavaScript can be used to extract and manipulate event field values, such as parsing a hostname from a complex event string. While JavaScript has other uses, parsing event data is the primary EM use case.

questions.stem: What would you use to define the monitoring sources allowed to communicate with the ServiceNow instance for Operational Intelligence?
questions.explanation: Metric Registration is used to define the monitoring sources allowed to communicate with the ServiceNow instance for Operational Intelligence. It registers which external metric sources can send data to the instance. Metric Config Rules map metrics to indicators, Metric Type Actions define actions on metric types, and Metric to CI binds metrics to configuration items.

questions.stem: The value of the Alert Priority score is a composite of what?

options.text: The value of the alert’s category and its relative weight
The value of the alert’s category and its Priority Group
The value of the alert’s Severity and its Priority Group
The value of the alert’s Severity and its relative weight

questions.explanation: Alert Priority score is a composite of the alert's Severity and its relative weight. The priority calculation uses severity as a primary factor, combined with weighted categories such as business services, CI type, and role. Each category has a score and a weight, but the core driver is the severity value multiplied by its weight position in the formula.

questions.stem: Which attribute is responsible for de-duplication?
questions.explanation: The Message_key attribute is responsible for de-duplication of events into alerts. When multiple events arrive with the same message_key value, they are consolidated into a single alert rather than creating separate alerts. The message_key uniquely identifies a condition so that duplicate events update the existing alert instead of generating new ones.

questions.stem: How would you interpret the following data in the Operational Intelligence Insights Explorer?

options.text: win-ces882ierw is one of your hottest Configuration Items (CIs) that is currently experiencing a high probability of anomalies and should be checked immediately
win-ces882ierw is one of your hottest Configuration Items (CIs), but is currently experiencing a low probability of anomalies
win-ces882ierw is one of your customized list of monitored Configuration Items (CIs) that is currently experiencing a high probability of anomalies and should be checked immediately
win-ces882ierw is one of your customized list of monitored Configuration Items (CIs), but is currently experiencing a low probability of anomalies

questions.explanation: In the Operational Intelligence Insights Explorer, win-ces882ierw being displayed as a 'hot' CI indicates it is currently experiencing a high probability of anomalies and should be checked immediately. The Insights Explorer uses color-coding and temperature metaphors to indicate anomaly severity — hotter CIs have higher anomaly scores requiring urgent attention.

questions.stem: What is the default collection/polling interval applied to all event connectors?
questions.explanation: The default collection/polling interval applied to all event connectors is every 40 seconds. This is the baseline frequency at which connectors poll their configured event sources for new events. Administrators can adjust this interval per connector based on the volume and urgency of events from each source.

questions.stem: Where can you look to determine what event rule created an alert? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To determine what event rule created an alert, you can look at Alert Activity (which logs processing actions including which rule was applied) and Event Processing Notes (which contain details about how the event was processed and which rules matched). The Alert Message Key and Alert Source identify the event origin, not the rule applied.

questions.stem: What feature would you use to trigger a workflow or automatically generate tasks via templates?
questions.explanation: Alert management rules are used to trigger a workflow or automatically generate tasks via templates. Alert management rules define automated responses to alerts, including launching remediation workflows, creating tasks from templates, and executing subflows. Event rules process incoming events, and alert correlation rules group related alerts.

questions.stem: What are the valid states an alert can be in during its lifecycle?
questions.explanation: The valid alert lifecycle states are Open, Reopen, Flapping, and Closed. An alert starts in Open state when created from events, can be Closed when the condition clears (severity 0/Clear), enters Flapping when it rapidly cycles between open and closed states, and moves to Reopen when a closed alert receives new events indicating the condition has returned.

questions.stem: What Event Management module allows for configuration of automatic task creation?
questions.explanation: Alert management rules is the Event Management module that allows configuration of automatic task creation. Alert management rules can be configured with Actions that automatically create tasks from templates when specific alert conditions are met. Task rules, Event rules, and Alert correlation rules serve different purposes in the EM pipeline.

questions.stem:
You have a system configured with a MID Web Server using Basic authentication to enable Operational Management Intelligence (OI) to push raw metric data to the MID Server. No data is getting through to the MID Server.
What is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The MID Web Server needs to be Restarted
The MID Web Server needs to be Started
An invalid secret key is being passed in the header information of the URL for the REST request
An invalid password is set in the MID Web Server Context

questions.explanation: With Basic authentication configured for the MID Web Server, the most likely cause of data not getting through is an invalid password set in the MID Web Server Configuration. Basic auth requires correct username/password credentials in the configuration. An invalid secret key would apply to token-based auth, and the MID Web Server would show errors if it needed restarting rather than silently dropping data.

questions.stem: In the event table, which field maps the external attributes from the target system?
questions.explanation: In the event table, the Additional Information field maps external attributes from the target system. This field is a JSON string that carries key-value pairs of extra data from the source monitoring system that does not map directly to standard event fields. The Resource field identifies what is affected, Source identifies where it came from, and Description is a text summary.

questions.stem: By default, the Alert Console displays what type of alerts?

options.text: All Primary, Open alerts and anomaly alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary and Secondary Open alerts and anomaly alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary, Open alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary and Secondary Open alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode

questions.explanation: By default, the Alert Console displays all Primary alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode. The default filter excludes Secondary alerts (child alerts within correlation groups), Clear severity alerts, and alerts on CIs in maintenance mode. Open and Reopen states are both included in this default view.

questions.stem: Which are recommended best practices for Event Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Filter out events on ServiceNow Instance for easier consolidation and aggregation.
Promote all events to alerts during initial implementation until you fully understand which should be ignored.
Filter out events at source rather than in the ServiceNow instance.
Base-line “normal-state” events to filter out background noise.
Ignore all non-critical events during initial implementation to streamline processing; add alerts over time as time and resources allow.

questions.explanation: Recommended best practices for Event Management include: Filter out events at source rather than in the ServiceNow instance (C) to reduce noise before it reaches the platform, Base-line normal-state events to filter out background noise (D) establishing a baseline of normal activity, and Filter out events on the ServiceNow instance for easier consolidation and aggregation (A). Promoting all events to alerts during initial implementation is NOT recommended as it creates excessive noise.

questions.stem: For an incoming event with a matching message key, what allows an existing alert to be automatically closed?

options.text: In the event rule, set the Severity to 0
In the alert rule, set the Severity to 0
In the alert rule, set the Severity to -1
In the event rule, set the Severity to -1

questions.explanation: To automatically close an existing alert when an incoming event with a matching message key arrives, set the Severity to 0/Clear in the event rule. A severity value of 0 or 'Clear' in an event signals that the condition has been resolved, causing the matching alert to transition to Closed state. Severity of -1 is not a valid value in standard Event Management.

questions.stem:
A support agent resolves an incident associated with an alert, but the alert does automatically close even though the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property is set appropriately to close the alert.
What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The support agent does not have the evt_mgmt_user role.
The support agent only has the evt_mgmt_admin role.
The support agent has the evt_mgmt_operator role, but not the evt_mgmt_user role.
The support agent has the evt_mgmt_user role, but not the evt_mgmt_operator role.

questions.explanation: The most likely cause is that the support agent has the evt_mgmt_user role but not the evt_mgmt_operator role. Closing an alert associated with an incident requires the evt_mgmt_operator role, which grants permissions to manipulate alert states. The evt_mgmt_user role alone provides read access but not the ability to close alerts through incident resolution.

questions.stem: What are the two most accurate statements regarding the ServiceNow CMDB (configuration management database) and CIs (configuration items)?

options.text: The CMDB is a series of tables that contain only key hardware components located in critical paths within your platform that must be managed.
The CMDB is a dynamic list that tracks both the CIs within your platform and the relationship between those items.
All CIs stored in the CMDB must have an assigned IP address within your infrastructure.
A CI is any component within your infrastructure that needs to be managed in order to deliver Services.

questions.explanation: The CMDB is a dynamic list that tracks both the CIs within your platform and the relationships between those items (B). A CI can be any manageable element including hardware, software, documentation, or services — it is not limited to hardware with IP addresses (D). The CMDB is not limited to key hardware components, and CIs do not require assigned IP addresses.

questions.stem: What would you use as a central location to explore the CMDB class hierarchy, CI table definitions, and CIs?
questions.explanation: CI Class Manager is the central location to explore the CMDB class hierarchy, CI table definitions, and CIs. It provides a unified interface to browse the CMDB class tree, view and edit table schemas, manage CI identifiers, and explore CI records. CI Remediations, Relation Types, and Identifiers are specific features, not comprehensive exploration tools.

questions.stem:
A four node cluster makes up the components (CIs) of a Business Service. The impact influence for the cluster is set to 60%.
How many members of the cluster must be in a Critical state in order for the Business Service to display as Critical in the Impact Tree?
questions.explanation: With a 4-node cluster and 60% impact influence, 3 members must be in Critical state. The formula is: required nodes = ceiling(cluster_size x influence_percentage). For a 4-node cluster at 60%: 4 x 0.60 = 2.4, rounded up to 3. When 3 of 4 nodes (75%) exceed the 60% threshold, the business service displays as Critical in the Impact Tree.

questions.stem: Which the following alert promotion rule defined in your ServiceNow instance, which of the anomalies below would be automatically promoted into IT alerts on the Alert Console?

options.text: Both anomaly A and anomaly B
Neither anomaly A or anomaly B

questions.explanation: Based on the exhibit context showing alert promotion rules and two anomalies, both anomaly A and anomaly B would be automatically promoted into IT alerts on the Alert Console. When alert promotion rules are configured to promote anomalies meeting certain criteria (like score thresholds or CI match), both anomalies that match the rule conditions are promoted.

questions.stem: By default, Event Management tries to bind an alert to CI (configuration item), by matching the node name in the event to which three items in the CMDB (configuration management database)?

options.text: CI name, Fully qualified domain name, IP or MAC address
CI name, Webserver name, IP or MAC address
CI name, Fully qualified domain name, SSH public host keys
System class name, Fully qualified domain name, IP or MAC address

questions.explanation: By default, Event Management tries to bind an alert to a CI by matching the node name in the event to three items in the CMDB: CI name, Fully qualified domain name (FQDN), and IP or MAC address. These three identifiers provide comprehensive matching — hostname, DNS name, and network address. Webserver name and SSH keys are not used in default CI binding.

questions.stem: The MID Server requires an outbound connection on which port?
questions.explanation: The MID Server requires an outbound connection on port 443 (HTTPS). The MID Server communicates with the ServiceNow instance over HTTPS, which uses port 443 for encrypted web traffic. Port 445 is for SMB/CIFS, port 161 is for SNMP, and port 143 is for IMAP email — none are used for MID Server to instance communication.

questions.stem: If more than one event rule applies to a particular event or metric, which of the event rules will run based upon the Order of execution number?

options.text: Only the event rule with the highest Order of execution number will run.
Only the event rule with the lowest Order of execution number will run.
All event rules will run, from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers.
All event rules will run, from the highest to the lowest Order of execution numbers.

questions.explanation: When multiple event rules apply to a particular event, all event rules will run from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers. Event rules are processed in ascending order — the rule with the lowest Order number executes first. All matching rules execute, not just one, allowing layered processing of events.

questions.stem: When creating event rules, is it best practice to create:
questions.explanation: When creating event rules, best practice is to create as few rules as possible. Each event rule adds processing overhead, so minimizing the number of rules improves performance and maintainability. Consolidate similar event handling logic into fewer, well-designed rules rather than creating individual rules for every event type.

questions.stem: During processing of the event and if the event Severity is blank, the state of the event is set to:
questions.explanation: During event processing, if the event Severity is blank (not provided), the state of the event is set to Error. Severity is a required field for event processing — without it, the system cannot determine the alert severity level and marks the event as Error. Events in Error state require manual review or rule adjustment to process correctly.

questions.stem: What two key steps must be performed after creating a new connector instance? (Choose two.)

options.text: Assign a MID Server to the connector

questions.explanation: After creating a new connector instance, the two key steps are Test the connector (to verify it can successfully communicate with the event source) and Activate the connector (to enable it to start collecting events). Testing validates the configuration works before activation, and activation starts the actual event collection process.

questions.stem:
A customer informs you that they already have monitoring and event management tools.
Which of the following describes the extra value that ServiceNow Event Management provides? (Choose four.)

options.text: ServiceNow Event Management Alerts, Incidents, Problems, and changes are automatically correlated with CIs and Business Services that can be visualized in Business Service maps.
ServiceNow Event Management manages relationships between alerts and related incidents to maintain an end-to-end event management lifecycle.
ServiceNow Event Management provides a business-centric platform and single system of record for service monitoring and remediation results, to better control and manage performance and availability.
ServiceNow Event Management provides state-of-the-art performance monitoring capabilities across a wide array of different types of infrastructures.

ServiceNow Event Management utilizes the power of MID Servers provide important functions in your ITOM Health deployment. What does MID stand for? A. Management, Instrumentation. and Discovery B. Messaging. Integration, and Data C. Monitoring. Insight. and Domain D. Maintenance, Information, and Distribution with leading monitoring systems to automatically create actionable alerts.

questions.explanation: ServiceNow Event Management provides extra value through: automatic correlation of Alerts, Incidents, Problems, and Changes with CIs and Business Services (A), managing relationships between alerts and related incidents end-to-end (B), and additional capabilities beyond what standalone monitoring tools provide. These represent the consolidation and service-aware context that traditional tools lack.

questions.stem: You have an event with a Source of ‘Trap from Enterprise 111’, but the alert created for this event shows a Source of ‘Oracle EM’. If you want to change what this is set to, where in the event rule would you do this?

options.text: Transform and Compose Alert Output lab

questions.explanation: To change what the Source value is set to on an alert, you configure this in the Transform and Compose Alert Output tab of the event rule. This tab controls how event field values are mapped and transformed into alert field values. You can override the Source field to display a more meaningful name (like 'Oracle EM') instead of the raw event source value.

questions.stem: Copies of checks that have been included in Agent Client Collector policies are known as what?
questions.explanation: Copies of checks that have been included in Agent Client Collector (ACC) policies are known as Check instances. When a check definition is added to a policy, the system creates a check instance — a copy of the check configured for that specific policy context. Check definitions are the templates, while check instances are the deployed copies within policies.

questions.stem: How often do baseline event connectors retrieve events?
questions.explanation: Baseline event connectors retrieve events every 2 minutes by default. This is the standard polling interval configured on out-of-the-box event connectors. The interval can be adjusted per connector based on the monitoring environment's needs, but 2 minutes is the default baseline for event collection frequency.

questions.stem: Which attribute correlates multiple events to one alert?
questions.explanation: The Message_key attribute correlates multiple events to one alert. Events with the same message_key value are consolidated into a single alert — new events update the existing alert rather than creating additional alerts. This deduplication mechanism prevents alert storms from repeated events about the same condition.

questions.stem: What attribute is used to consolidate events into a single alert?
questions.explanation: The Message Key attribute is used to consolidate events into a single alert. When multiple events share the same Message Key value, they are grouped and update a single alert record. This is the core deduplication mechanism in Event Management — without matching message keys, each event would create a separate alert.

questions.stem: Which attribute within an event needs to be exactly the same to allow for deduplication?
questions.explanation: The Message Key attribute must be exactly the same across events for deduplication to occur. Events with identical message key values are treated as duplicates and consolidated into a single alert. Other fields like Metric Name, Type, Node, and Description may vary between deduplicated events — only the message key must match exactly.

questions.stem: In default configuration using baseline connectors, how often is event data collected from event sources?
questions.explanation: In default configuration using baseline connectors, event data is collected from event sources once every minute (60 seconds). This is the standard polling frequency for baseline connectors. The interval balances timely event detection with reasonable resource consumption on both the MID Server and source systems.

questions.stem: What applications are included in the ITOM Health product?
questions.explanation: ITOM Health includes Event Management and Operational Intelligence. These two applications form the ITOM Health product, providing event correlation, alert management, anomaly detection, and metric-based operational insights. ITOM Visibility includes Discovery and Service Mapping. Cloud Management is a separate ITOM product.

questions.stem: What is one of the main benefits of using Event Management and Operational Intelligence?

options.text: To improve service availability by helping IT staff pinpoint service issue causes and evaluate the impact of planned changes.
To increase service agility and produce fast, predictable results by automating manual, routine, error-prone tasks.
To rapidly configure and launch secure, agentless discovery of hardware and software resources and their relationships.
To proactively warn against possible service outages using a range of advanced predictive machine learning methods.

questions.explanation: A main benefit of Event Management and Operational Intelligence is to proactively warn against possible service issues before they cause outages. OI uses machine learning to detect anomalies in operational metrics, providing early warning of degrading conditions. Option A describes Service Mapping impact analysis, B describes orchestration, and C describes Discovery.

questions.stem:
MID Servers provide important functions in your ITOM Health deployment.
What does MID stand for?
questions.explanation: MID stands for Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery. The MID Server facilitates communication between a ServiceNow instance and external applications, data sources, and services within the customer's network. It manages connections, instruments monitoring, and supports discovery operations.

questions.stem: Out-of-the-box, how often do the events get processed in ServiceNow?

options.text: Every minute via a scheduled job
As soon as the event record is inserted via a business rule

questions.explanation: Out-of-the-box, events get processed in ServiceNow every 5 seconds. The event processing scheduled job runs at a 5-second interval, picking up new events from the em_event table and processing them through the event pipeline (filtering, binding, alert creation/update). This rapid processing ensures near-real-time alert generation.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
In what sequence are events processed?
questions.explanation: Events are processed in a specific sequence: first through Event Rules (filtering and transformation), then Alert creation/update via Message Key matching, followed by CI Binding (matching to CMDB), and finally Alert Actions (management rules, correlation). This pipeline ensures events are properly classified before being promoted to alerts.

questions.stem: Which is not a valid method for accessing alert intelligence?

options.text: In the right-click menu of an alert list, select Open in Workspace
By appending/workspace to your instance URL
The application navigator Alerts Console menu item
The application navigator Alert Intelligence menu item
Within an open alert record, click the Open in Workspace button
Select the Lists tab in operator workspace

questions.explanation: Selecting the Lists tab in operator workspace is not a valid method for accessing alert intelligence. Valid methods include the right-click menu Open in Workspace, appending /workspace to the URL, the Alerts Console navigator item, the Alert Intelligence navigator item, and the Open in Workspace button within an alert record.

questions.stem: To determine the top incidents for the CI associated with an alert, where is the best place to look?
questions.explanation: Alert Insights is the best place to determine the top incidents for the CI associated with an alert. Alert Insights provides contextual information including related incidents, changes, and problems for the CI bound to the alert. This gives operators immediate visibility into CI history without leaving the alert context.

questions.stem: Agent Client Collector is built on what framework that enables you to adopt and extend monitoring checks from the community?
questions.explanation: Agent Client Collector is built on the Sensu framework, which enables you to adopt and extend monitoring checks from the community. Sensu is an open-source monitoring framework with a large community library of checks and plugins. ACC leverages Sensu's architecture for executing checks on endpoints. Nagios, Icinga, Zabbix, and SolarWinds are alternative monitoring tools not used by ACC.

questions.stem: Based on the information shown, which of the following three alerts should be processed first?

options.text:
The Alert Priority score 3106020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-06-01 19:34:01 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (3.0, 1000000)
2. Severity – (1.0, 100000)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100)
4. Role – (2.0, 10)
5. Secondary – (0)
6. State – (1.0, 0.001)

The Alert Priority score 4406020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-05-31 20:04:47 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (4.0, 1000000.0)
2. Severity – (4.0, 100000.0)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100.0)
4. Role – (2.0, 10.0)
5. Secondary – (0)
6. State – (1.0, 0.001)

The Alert Priority score 3306020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-05-31 19:56:54 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (3.0, 1000000.0)
2. Severity – (3.0, 100000.0)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100.0)
4. Role – (2.0, 10.0)

6. State – (1.0, 0.001)
They should be processed in the order in which they were received.

questions.explanation: Among the three alerts, the one with Alert Priority score 4406020.001 should be processed first because it has the highest priority score. Alert Priority is a numerical score — higher values indicate higher priority. The scoring factors (Business services, Severity, CI type, Role, Secondary, State) are weighted and summed, with the highest total score receiving attention first.

questions.stem: Applying recommended Event Management best practice guidelines, which of the following events should generate an alert?

options.text: Every event should generate an alert so you have the opportunity to resolve them all.
Only events that necessitate action should generate an alert.
Only the most critical events on every CI in the CMDB should generate an alert.
Every event on every critical CI in the CMDB should generate an alert.

questions.explanation: Applying Event Management best practice guidelines, only events that necessitate action should generate an alert. Not every event warrants attention — many events are informational or represent normal operations. By promoting only actionable events to alerts, you reduce alert fatigue and ensure operators focus on conditions that require response.

questions.stem: What makes all ServiceNow metrics, tasks, services, configuration items, assets, people, locations, and information a single system of record for IT and business processes?

options.text: ServiceNow is installed within your datacenter providing you complete control
All applications are built on the Oracle database standard, providing uniformity across products
All applications that are built by ServiceNow utilize the same data model and code base
ServiceNow runs on supported Windows servers and is managed through Windows Update
A single table houses all data elements within ServiceNow
ServiceNow utilizes the AWS MariaDB cloud database structure, providing a single system of record

questions.explanation: All applications built by ServiceNow utilize the same data model and code base, making it a single system of record for IT and business processes. This unified platform architecture means metrics, tasks, services, CIs, assets, people, locations, and information all share a common foundation. ServiceNow is cloud-hosted (not on-premises), and uses its own database (not Oracle).

questions.stem:
You have a very large networking environment and have noticed that your event notifications are either not being triggered or are delayed.
What are best options to try to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure all Event Management – process events jobs are set to a Ready state
Verify that the Bucket field in the event table is set to zero (0)
Ensure multi-node event processing is disabled

questions.explanation: To resolve delayed or missing event notifications in a large networking environment: ensure all Event Management process events jobs are set to a Ready state (A) so they are actively processing, and add additional event processor jobs (C) to handle the higher event volume. More processor jobs distribute the workload across threads. Disabling multi-node processing would reduce capacity, not improve it.

questions.stem: What event value will auto close an alert?
questions.explanation: An event with Severity of 0/Clear will auto-close an alert. When an incoming event has severity value 0 (also labeled 'Clear'), it signals that the monitored condition has returned to normal. The system matches the event to its associated alert via message key and transitions the alert to Closed state. Severity -1 and Resolution States are not used for auto-closure.

questions.stem: Given the following Impact settings and Alerts in a three node cluster that makes up the components of a Business Service, what is the overall service health of this Business Service?
questions.explanation: Based on the exhibit showing a 3-node cluster with specific impact settings and alert conditions, the overall service health would be Minor. The number of impacted nodes relative to the cluster influence percentage determines the service degradation level. With fewer nodes impacted than the influence threshold, the service shows a lower severity than Critical.

questions.stem: What does Operational Intelligence proactively identify before they cause service outages?
questions.explanation: Operational Intelligence proactively identifies Anomalies before they cause service outages. OI uses machine learning algorithms to analyze metric data patterns and detect deviations from normal behavior (anomalies). These anomalies serve as early warning indicators of potential issues. Missing CMDB data, defects, alert correlations, and orphaned CIs are not what OI proactively identifies.

questions.stem: What is the function of the External Communication Channel (ECC) Queue? (Choose three.)

options.text: It is a connection point between a ServiceNow instance and the MID Server.
It contains probe records to be executed on the customer’s network.
It holds jobs that the MID Server needs to perform.
It is a connection point between a hardware CI on a customer’s network and the MID Server.
It contains records of CIs that the ServiceNow admin has submitted for entry into the CMDB.

questions.explanation: The ECC Queue serves three functions: it is a connection point between a ServiceNow instance and the MID Server (A), it contains probe records to be executed on the customer's network (B), and it holds jobs that the MID Server needs to perform (C). It is NOT a connection between hardware CIs and the MID Server, nor does it hold CI entry records submitted by admins.

questions.stem: The correct regex to capture the name of the server in “the server webserver3.domain.com is down” would be:
questions.explanation: The regex .*\s(\w+\.\w+\.\w+).* correctly captures 'webserver3.domain.com' from the string 'the server webserver3.domain.com is down'. The pattern matches: any characters, a whitespace, then captures a word-dot-word-dot-word pattern (the server FQDN), followed by any remaining characters. Option A's .* before the capture group would greedily consume too much.

questions.stem: What is the recommended approach to normalizing data from a source system to the default values in Event Management?
questions.explanation: Event field mapping is the recommended approach to normalizing data from a source system to the default values in Event Management. Event field mapping defines how source-specific field names and values translate to standard ServiceNow event fields, ensuring consistent data format across different monitoring tools. Transform maps handle data imports, not real-time event normalization.

questions.stem:
You have an event that needs to be bound to a non-host CI.
Which attribute needs to be removed from the Transform and Compose tab?
questions.explanation: When binding an event to a non-host CI, the Node attribute needs to be removed from the Transform and Compose tab. By default, CI binding matches the Node field to host CIs in the CMDB. For non-host CIs (applications, services, etc.), removing Node prevents incorrect host-level matching and allows the binding to use other attributes like Resource.

questions.stem: When are anomaly alerts generated by Operational Intelligence displayed in alert intelligence?

options.text: When the statistical model threshold is breached
When they are promoted to IT alerts
When it is manually promoted in insights explorer
When the anomaly score is greater than 100

questions.explanation: Anomaly alerts generated by Operational Intelligence are displayed in alert intelligence when they are promoted to IT alerts. Anomalies detected by OI exist as anomaly records initially. Only when they meet promotion criteria and are promoted to IT alerts do they appear in the Alert Intelligence workspace alongside standard alerts.

questions.stem: What are the possible actions available in alert management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The possible actions available in alert management are: Execute remediation subflows (A), Execute remediation workflows (B), and Launch applications (C). These three action types automate alert response — subflows and workflows run automated remediation, while Launch applications opens external tools. Evaluate business rule and Create service catalog request are not alert management actions.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature would you configure to process incoming email to create events?
questions.explanation: Inbound actions (also known as inbound email actions) are the ServiceNow feature configured to process incoming email to create events. Inbound actions monitor a mailbox and can parse incoming emails to create event records in the em_event table based on email content. Transforms handle data imports, and Event filter/field mapping process events after creation.

questions.stem: Within a PowerShell script, which two URI’s could you use to log events directly to the ServiceNow event table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Within a PowerShell script, two valid URIs for logging events to the ServiceNow event table are: the em/jsonv2 endpoint (B) which is the Event Management-specific REST API, and the standard Table API (C) /api/now/table/em_event which can create records in any table. The other URI formats are incorrect ServiceNow REST API paths.

questions.stem: If more than one alert management rule applies to a particular alert, which of the rules will run based upon the Order of execution field?

options.text: Only the alert management rule with the highest Order of execution number will run.
Only the alert management rule with the lowest Order of execution number will run.
All alert management rules will run, from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers.
All alert management rules will run, from the highest to the lowest Order of execution numbers.

questions.explanation: When multiple alert management rules apply, all rules will run from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers. Similar to event rules, alert management rules process in ascending order of their Order field value. All matching rules execute sequentially, allowing layered alert processing. Only-one-runs behavior does not apply to alert management rules.

questions.stem: Alerts are processed using which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Alerts are processed using alert management rules (A) which define automated responses, event rules (C) which determine how events become alerts and set alert properties, and scheduled jobs (D) which handle periodic alert maintenance like closing idle alerts and processing flapping states. Event action rules and Java/Groovy scripts are not standard alert processing mechanisms.

questions.stem: The individual commands that the Agent Client Collector executes on the host are known as what? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The individual commands that Agent Client Collector executes on the host are known as Checks (B), Metrics (E), and Scripts (F). Checks are monitoring commands that evaluate system state, Metrics collect performance data values, and Scripts execute custom monitoring logic. Events are outputs, Policies are collections of checks, and Parameters are configuration settings.

questions.stem: What is Event Management licensing based on?

options.text: The number of unique nodes that can send events to the instance
The number of connectors and listeners it will collect data from
The number of connectors it will collect data from
The number of CIs in the CMDB that it will be monitoring

questions.explanation: Event Management licensing is based on the number of unique nodes that can send events to the instance. Each unique node (identified by its node name in events) counts toward the license. Licensing is not based on the number of connectors, listeners, or CMDB CIs — only the distinct event-sending nodes matter.

questions.stem: What missing attribute would cause an event to have a state of Error?
questions.explanation: A missing Source attribute would cause an event to have a state of Error during processing. Source is a required field for event processing — it identifies where the event originated. Without a Source value, the event processing engine cannot properly categorize or handle the event and marks it as Error. Node, Severity, and Metric Name have different handling when missing.

questions.stem: Modified Agent Client Collector policies do not take effect until what action is taken?

options.text: The check is tested on an existing agent/host

questions.explanation: Modified Agent Client Collector policies do not take effect until the policy is republished. After making changes to an ACC policy (adding/removing checks, changing parameters), the policy must be explicitly republished to push the updated configuration to agents. Restarting agents, running discovery, or MID server sync are not the mechanism for applying policy changes.

questions.stem: What does the Asynchronous Messaging Bus (AMB) channel do on the MID Server?

options.text: Opens an inbound connection to the MID Server
Allows Web Server transactions to be passed to ServiceNow
Sends heartbeat information to the ServiceNow instance to ensure MID is communicating
Continually queries the External Communication Channel (ECC) queue via a persistent query

questions.explanation: The Asynchronous Messaging Bus (AMB) channel on the MID Server continually queries the External Communication Channel (ECC) queue via a persistent query. AMB replaced the older polling mechanism, providing real-time notification when new ECC Queue records are available for the MID Server. This persistent connection reduces latency compared to periodic polling.

questions.stem: Within the ServiceNow IT Operations Management solution set, which statement most accurately describes what Event Management is?

options.text: The process responsible for defining, analyzing, planning, measuring, and improving all aspects of the availability of IT services
The process responsible for ensuring the capacity of IT Services and IT infrastructure is able to deliver agreed upon service level targets in a cost-effective manner
The process responsible for monitoring all abnormal occurrences throughout the IT infrastructure, allowing for normal operations, and detecting and escalating exception conditions
The process responsible for recovery action and planning through machine learning

questions.explanation: Event Management is the process responsible for monitoring all abnormal occurrences from monitoring systems, correlating them, determining their impact, and triggering appropriate responses. It manages the lifecycle of events from collection through alert creation and resolution. Options A and B describe Availability Management and Capacity Management respectively.

questions.stem: When creating a task from an alert what Event Management Module would be used?
questions.explanation: Alert Management is the Event Management module used when creating a task from an alert. Alert Management rules can be configured to automatically or manually create tasks (incidents, problems, changes) from alerts. Event Rules handle event processing, Alert Correlation groups related alerts, and Task Management is not a specific EM module.

questions.stem: What is the preferred method of parsing in the Transform/Compose step of an event rule?
questions.explanation: JavaScript is the preferred method of parsing in the Transform/Compose step of an event rule. ServiceNow uses JavaScript as its primary scripting language for field transformations and data manipulation. In the Transform and Compose tab, JavaScript expressions and functions extract, modify, and compose alert field values from raw event data. Python, regex, and sed/awk are not the preferred method.

questions.stem: What are the server requirements to allow Operational Intelligence to successfully collect operational metric data via a push?

options.text: This requires a minimum of three MID Servers - two for Event Management and one additional MID Server dedicated for use by Operational Intelligence (OI).
This requires a MID Web Server in addition to the MID Server.
Nothing additional is required; this is handled by the MID Server.
This requires a minimum of two MID Servers - one for Event Management and one additional MID Server dedicated for use by Operational Intelligence (OI).

questions.explanation: To successfully collect operational metric data via a push, Operational Intelligence requires a MID Web Server in addition to the MID Server. The MID Web Server provides an HTTP/HTTPS endpoint that external monitoring tools can push metric data to. The MID Server alone only supports pull-based collection. A MID Web Server is a separate component that receives pushed data.

questions.stem: What would be an appropriate use case for having to write JavaScript in Event Management?

options.text: To change the value of the message key
To create a custom action within a subflow
To parse a node name out of your raw event data in an event rule

questions.explanation: An appropriate use case for writing JavaScript in Event Management is to parse a node name out of raw event data in an event rule. The Transform and Compose tab of event rules supports JavaScript for extracting specific values from complex event strings. Changing message keys, creating custom subflow actions, and auto-creating incidents use other mechanisms (rule configuration, Flow Designer, alert management rules).

questions.stem: A dynamic grouping of CIs based upon common criteria (filtered CI classes) that can be visualized in operator workspace is called?
questions.explanation: A dynamic grouping of CIs based upon common criteria (filtered CI classes) that can be visualized in operator workspace is called a Technical Service. Technical services are dynamically assembled groups of CIs based on filters and criteria, as opposed to Application Services (discovered by Service Mapping) or Manual Services (manually defined). Business services are broader organizational constructs.

questions.stem: During CI binding, CI matching is done using which two fields? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: During CI Binding, CI matching is done using the Source and Node fields from the event record. The Node value is matched against CI name, FQDN, and IP/MAC address in the CMDB, while Source helps identify the monitoring system. Message Key is for deduplication, and Additional Information carries supplementary data not used for primary CI matching.

questions.stem: What three areas of data quality does the CMDB Health Dashboard focus on? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB Health Dashboard focuses on three areas of data quality: Correctness (accuracy of CI data, including duplicate and stale detection), Completeness (how thoroughly CI records are populated with required/recommended attributes), and Compliance (whether CIs meet defined relationship and attribute requirements). Configuration, Conciseness, and Conformity are not CMDB Health KPIs.

questions.stem: When sending data from the monitoring source to the additional_info field, what format is supported?
questions.explanation: When sending data from a monitoring source to the additional_info field, JSON format is supported. The additional_info field accepts JSON strings containing key-value pairs of supplementary event data. For example: {"CPU":"100","Status":"3"}. XML, YAML, and comma-separated formats are not supported for the additional_info field.

questions.stem: Which step in the event rule configuration process enables you to ignore events and prevent alert generation?
questions.explanation: The Event Filter step in the event rule configuration enables you to ignore events and prevent alert generation. The Event Filter tab defines conditions that determine whether an event should be processed or discarded. Events matching filter conditions set to 'Ignore' are not promoted to alerts. Transform and Compose handles field mapping, not filtering.

questions.stem: What is an alert called that moves from an open to a closed state multiple times within a designated time-frame?
questions.explanation: An alert that moves from an open to a closed state multiple times within a designated time-frame is called Flapping. Flapping indicates the monitored condition is unstable — it keeps clearing and reoccurring rapidly. ServiceNow detects flapping based on configurable frequency and interval properties (evt_mgmt.flap_frequency and evt_mgmt.flap_interval).

questions.stem: How would you ensure the quality of data in your Configuration Management Database (CMDB) over time?

options.text: Manually inventorying configuration items in the CMDB and eliminating duplicate configuration items (CIs)
Only use the ServiceNow Discovery application to populate your CMDB
Using only scripts to automatically monitor for and remediate duplicate configuration items (CIs)
Having well-defined Identification, Reconciliation, and Relationship rules

questions.explanation: Having well-defined Identification, Reconciliation, and Relationship rules ensures CMDB data quality over time. These IRE rules automate CI identity matching, attribute reconciliation across data sources, and relationship maintenance. Manual inventorying is impractical at scale, relying solely on Discovery misses manually managed CIs, and scripts alone cannot comprehensively enforce data quality.

questions.stem: Which is an invalid state for an alert?
questions.explanation: Processed is an invalid state for an alert. The valid alert lifecycle states are Open, Reopen, Flapping, and Closed. An alert transitions between these states based on incoming events and configured properties. 'Processed' is an event state (events move through Ready, Processed, Error states), not an alert state.

questions.stem: A support agent resolves an incident associated with an alert. What is the best method to close the alert?

options.text: Switch over to the alert form and close the alert manually
Create a business rule on the alert table to match the associated Incident with its respective alert
Create a business rule on the incident table

questions.explanation: The best method to close an alert when its associated incident is resolved is to set the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property to true. This system property creates an automatic link between incident resolution and alert closure. When enabled, resolving or closing the incident automatically closes the associated alert. Manual closure and custom business rules are less maintainable approaches.

questions.stem: Impacted services for alerts are calculated using data from which table?
questions.explanation: Impacted services for alerts are calculated using data from the svc_ci_assoc table. This table stores Service-to-CI associations that define which CIs are components of which services. When an alert fires on a CI, the system queries svc_ci_assoc to determine which services are impacted. cmdb_ci_hardware stores hardware CIs, and em_impacted_svc stores the calculated results.

questions.stem: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as what?
questions.explanation: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as an Event. In ServiceNow Event Management terminology, an event is a raw notification from a monitoring tool about something that happened in the monitored environment. Events are processed and may be promoted to alerts if they require attention. Alerts are derived from events, metrics are numerical measurements, and alarms are monitoring-tool-specific.

questions.stem: If a Message Key is not provided, which fields are concatenated to make our own?

options.text: Source, DNS, Node, Additional info, Metric Name
Source, Type, Node, Resource, Metric Name
Source, Type, DNS, Additional info, Metric Name
Source, Source Instance, Node, Type, Resource

questions.explanation: If a Message Key is not provided, the default value is created by concatenating: Source, Type, Node, Resource, and Metric Name. These five fields are combined to create a unique identifier for event deduplication. This ensures events from the same source about the same resource on the same node are properly consolidated into a single alert.

questions.stem: A load balanced web application has a cluster of 5 Apache nodes. When considering impact calculation with application cluster member rule influence set to 45, how many impacted nodes within that cluster would cause the overall application service to have a degradation of service?
questions.explanation: With a 5-node Apache cluster and application cluster member rule influence set to 45 (meaning 45% of nodes must be impacted), 3 impacted nodes would cause degradation. The calculation: 5 x 0.45 = 2.25 nodes. Since 2 impacted nodes (40%) is below the threshold and 3 impacted nodes (60%) exceeds it, 3 nodes must be impacted for service degradation.

questions.stem: A Service is not viewable in Operator Workspace. What could be the issue?

options.text: The service is a manual service
The service is not set to operational
The service was created through Service Mapping
The service is a technical service

questions.explanation: If a Service is not viewable in Operator Workspace, the most likely issue is that the service is not set to operational. Services must have their operational status set to 'Operational' to appear in the Operator Workspace. Manual services, services from Service Mapping, and technical services can all appear in Operator Workspace when properly configured and set to operational.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature is an aid to rapid implementation of your Event Management and Operational Intelligence features?
questions.explanation: Guided Setup is the ServiceNow feature that aids rapid implementation of Event Management and Operational Intelligence features. Guided Setup provides step-by-step wizard-like guidance for configuring connectors, event rules, alert management rules, and OI settings. It walks administrators through the required setup tasks in the correct order.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow standard and shared set of service-related definitions that enable and support true service level reporting is known as what?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is ServiceNow's standard and shared set of service-related definitions that enable and support true service level reporting. CSDM provides a consistent framework for modeling business services, application services, and technical services across the platform. It standardizes how services are represented and related.

questions.stem: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as what?
questions.explanation: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as an Event. This is the same concept as Q82 — in ServiceNow terminology, events are the raw notifications received from monitoring tools. They are the starting point of the Event Management pipeline, processed through rules before potentially becoming alerts. Alarms, alerts, incidents, and metrics serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Which is the best option to reduce latency issues when receiving events?

options.text: Verify bucket field in em_event table > 0

questions.explanation: To reduce latency issues when receiving events, verify the bucket field in the em_event table is greater than 0. The bucket field controls event processing distribution across multiple processor jobs. When set to 0, all events go to a single processor. Values greater than 0 enable multi-processor distribution, reducing latency under high event volumes.

questions.stem: The default polling time to collect events from an event source is:
questions.explanation: The default polling time to collect events from an event source is 60 seconds. Event connectors poll their configured monitoring sources at this interval by default. This one-minute frequency provides a reasonable balance between timely event collection and resource usage. Administrators can adjust this per connector for specific monitoring needs.

questions.stem: Which two methods can be used to improve the processing of events in large network environments? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure the bucket value in the event table is greater than 0
Increase the number of scheduled jobs processing events

questions.explanation: Two methods to improve event processing in large network environments are: Enable multi-node processing (A) which distributes event processing across multiple application nodes, and Increase the number of scheduled jobs processing events (D) which adds more concurrent processing threads. Multi-node processing leverages clustered instances, and more jobs handle higher event volumes.

questions.stem: The Event Management operator workspace can display all of the following except?

options.text: Discovered application services from Service Mapping

questions.explanation: The Event Management operator workspace can display all of the listed options except Manual application services. Operator Workspace can show Alert groups, Discovered application services from Service Mapping, Correlation groups, and Technical services. Manual application services are not automatically visualized in the Operator Workspace as they lack the dynamic mapping that discovered services have.

questions.stem: Within an event rule, how would you parse a nodename out of your raw event data?
questions.explanation: Within an event rule, a Regex (regular expression) statement is used to parse a nodename out of raw event data. In the Transform and Compose tab, regex patterns extract specific values from event field strings. While JavaScript is also available, regex is the direct parsing mechanism referenced in this context. Groovy and PowerShell are not used within event rules.

questions.stem: If events are not matching to alerts as you would like, what field should be changed?
questions.explanation: If events are not matching to alerts as expected, the Message Key field should be changed. The message key determines how events are deduplicated and matched to existing alerts. If events that should update the same alert have different message keys, they create separate alerts. Adjusting the message key composition ensures proper event-to-alert matching.

questions.stem: If the Message Key is not populated, the default value is created from which fields?

options.text: Source, type. node, resource, and metric name
Source, source instance, node, and resource
Source, type. node, and metric name
Source, source instance, node, and type
Source, type. node, resource, and time of event

questions.explanation: If the Message Key is not populated, the default value is created from Source, Type, Node, Resource, and Metric Name fields. These five fields are concatenated to generate a unique message key for event deduplication. This default ensures that events from the same source about the same condition on the same node are properly consolidated.

questions.stem: Processing on an event will create a state of error if what value is not set?
questions.explanation: Processing on an event will create a state of Error if the Source value is not set. Source is a mandatory field for event processing — it identifies the monitoring system that generated the event. Without a Source, the event processing engine cannot determine the event origin and marks the event as Error for manual review.

questions.stem: When performing CI Binding, what fields does Event Management match to the Node?

options.text: CI Name, DNS, IP, MAC Address
System class name, FQDN, IP or MAC address
CI name, FQDN, SSH public host keys
CI Name, FQDN, IP, MAC Address

questions.explanation: When performing CI Binding, Event Management matches the Node field to: CI Name, FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name), IP, and MAC Address. These four identifiers provide comprehensive matching to locate the correct CI in the CMDB. System class name and SSH public host keys are not used in standard CI binding matching.

questions.stem: Applying recommended Event Management best practice guidelines, which of the following alerts should be processed first?
questions.explanation: Applying Event Management best practice, Alert0010003 should be processed first because it has the highest alert priority score. Alert priority is calculated from weighted factors including business services, severity, CI type, and role. The alert with the highest composite score deserves first attention. Without seeing exact scores, lower numbers in the alert name don't indicate priority — the calculated score does.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role needed to view alerts?
questions.explanation: The minimum role needed to view alerts is evt_mgmt_user. This role provides read access to the alerts list and individual alert records. The evt_mgmt_operator role provides additional capabilities like acknowledging and managing alerts, while evt_mgmt_admin provides full configuration access. alert_operator and alert_user are not standard Event Management roles.

questions.stem: By default, when are idle alerts are closed?
questions.explanation: By default, idle alerts are closed after 7 days. The system runs a scheduled job that checks for alerts that haven't received new events within the idle period. Alerts that remain unchanged for 7 days are automatically transitioned to Closed state. This prevents stale alerts from cluttering the Alert Console.

questions.stem: What is used to correctly bind an alert to an application?
questions.explanation: CI identification rules are used to correctly bind an alert to an application. CI identification rules define how the system matches event data to specific CI records in the CMDB, including application CIs. These rules use attributes like name, IP, FQDN to locate the correct CI. Correlation rules group alerts, workflows automate tasks, and classifiers categorize Discovery results.

questions.stem: If you wanted to create a quick response alert rule to open an Ask Jeeves search on the description of the alert, where would it configured?
questions.explanation: Launch Applications is where you would configure a quick response alert rule to open an external search (like Ask Jeeves) on the description of an alert. The Launch Applications action in alert management rules allows opening external URLs or applications, passing alert field values (like description) as parameters. Remediation Workflows and SubFlows handle automated fixes, not external app launches.

questions.stem: Where would you find the Priority Breakdown for an Alert?
questions.explanation: The Priority Breakdown for an Alert is found under the More Information section. This section displays the detailed breakdown of how the alert priority score was calculated, showing each category (Business services, Severity, CI type, Role, Secondary, State) with its individual score and weight contribution.

questions.stem: Where does an operator give feedback on an automated alert grouping?

options.text: Feedback attribute on the virtual alert record
Feedback attribute on the child alert record
Feedback attribute on the event record
Feedback attribute on the alert record
Dropdown box on the alert group record

questions.explanation: An operator gives feedback on an automated alert grouping through a Dropdown box on the alert group record. The alert group record provides a feedback mechanism where operators can indicate whether the automated grouping was helpful, accurate, or needs adjustment. This feedback helps improve the machine learning models used for future alert groupings.

questions.stem: In your environment, no alert CMDB, automated, or text based grouping is occurring. What is most likely the problem?

options.text: No correlation rules have been defined
No event management rules have been defined
The alert correlation property that enables grouping is set to false

questions.explanation: If no alert CMDB, automated, or text-based grouping is occurring, the most likely problem is that the alert correlation property that enables grouping is set to false. Alert grouping must be explicitly enabled via the evt_mgmt.enable_alert_grouping property. Without this property set to true, none of the grouping mechanisms (CMDB-based, automated, or text-based) will function.

questions.stem: The additional information field is a JSON string that gives more information about an event. An example of a supported JSON string is:
questions.explanation: A supported JSON string for the additional_info field is {"CPU":"100"}. In the additional_info field, all values should be strings enclosed in double quotes, and all keys must use double quotes (not single quotes). Option B uses a single quote for 'Status' which is invalid JSON. Option C mixes string and number values. Option A has an unquoted number value but is technically valid JSON — however D with consistent string formatting is the example shown.

questions.stem: In order for SNMP trap notifications to appear in ServiceNow as events, what option must be enabled in the required MID server?

options.text: SNMP event manager module for MID

questions.explanation: For SNMP trap notifications to appear in ServiceNow as events, the MID SNMP trap listener option must be enabled on the MID Server. The SNMP trap listener extension configures the MID Server to listen for incoming SNMP trap messages on the standard SNMP trap port (162) and convert them into ServiceNow events.

questions.stem: What event will cause Agent Client Collector self-monitoring to pause data collection?

options.text: Communication with the MID server is lost
The amount of host memory being used by the agent exceeds a threshold
Communication with the ServiceNow instance is lost
The amount of host disk space used by the agent exceeds a threshold
The amount of host CPU being utilized by the agent exceeds a threshold

questions.explanation: Agent Client Collector self-monitoring pauses data collection when the amount of host memory being used by the agent exceeds a threshold. ACC monitors its own resource consumption to prevent excessive impact on the host system. When memory usage exceeds the configured threshold, data collection pauses to protect host performance until memory usage drops below the threshold.

questions.stem: Agent Client Collector can perform application service monitoring by configuring what option?
questions.explanation: Agent Client Collector can perform application service monitoring by configuring a proxy agent. A proxy agent enables ACC to monitor application services by acting as an intermediary for service endpoint checks. This extends ACC's capabilities beyond host-level monitoring to service-level monitoring without requiring direct agent installation on every application component.
